source: My Draft Strategy (p11, Joel Smyth's Draft Guide 2026)
note: His median desired draft by position for 12-team PPR; Best Player Available still most important.
rules: Don't draft off rankings without understanding ADP - use rankings to find value, don't take a player 62nd who goes 85th on average.
"Don't Beat ADP" - the goal isn't drafting RB30 to have them finish RB29; take the riskier, upside player if true value potential is higher.
No K or D/ST until the last two rounds unless you wanna intimidate everyone.
Good "Process Players" late - rookie WRs, rushing QBs, talent on top offenses, cemented RB2s/handcuffs at end of drafts.
Balance risk - don't draft Nabers, Love, & Kittle on the same team.
Early waivers & even post-draft waivers matter the most they will all season.

QB.main: Main Target - ADP QB7-11: sniping one of your favorites that falls, mostly 2-3 still available in Round 8.
QB.secondary: Late rushing QB - 70% of the time, it works every time. I'd include Purdy/Nix as volume QBs.
QB.note: QB 3-6 are going WAY later this year; still would rather wait, but if one falls far it's likely worth it (QB3 2026 - 55th overall, QB6 2025 - 59th overall).

RB.main: Main Target - Getting 3 RB of top ~25-30. RB/RB is great; the elite league winners are in Rounds 1-2 90% of the time.
RB.note: RB30-40 is mostly a waste of time compared to that range's QB/WR/TE.

WR.main: Main Target - Round 3 & 5 WR range; as a whole, prefer over most RBs.
WR.note: The WR5-12 range usually is not my favorite compared to both the RBs in their round & WRs a round later. WRs are the most ideal position when hunting upside late in drafts.

TE.main: Main Target - Waiting for Best Value. Can get behind all ranges this year; want TE when it's best player available.
TE.note: Like TE2-4 if no favorite RB/WR available; Rd 7/8 grab one of the last mid-round TEs once RB/WR is dried up; punting completely strategically works. Rather go backup RB hunting than grabbing a TE2.
